title: School Notebooks 5-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Two prior weeks with same price: sales dropped to 10 and 7 (vs baseline 7.7), implying demand elasticity.

drivers.name: Competitor store opening across the street
drivers.evidence: No prior data on competitor entry, but store closures and new competitors are known demand reducers; credible but untested.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 7.7. No events or promotions are planned, but the price increased by 2.3% to $9.03. A competitor opens across the street, likely reducing demand. Past price increases (e.g., 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) showed no lift—sales dropped to 10 and 7, vs baseline 7.7, suggesting price sensitivity. The noise-adjusted effect of past promotions is weak (x1.16), and no post-promo dip is observed. The competitor opening is a credible downside driver. Evidence is limited (one past price hike, one new competitor), so shrink toward 1.0. No seasonality or trend supports uplift. The baseline already reflects back-to-school ramp-up, which ended. Adjust down slightly.

brief:
PRODUCT: School Notebooks 5-pack | category Office | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 9.03 (+2.3% vs regular price 8.83)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.7 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 33.1 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 21.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
